headline: High: agentic-flow can write/egress and use MCP, while ai-engineering-hub is non-egress; pairwise risks center on prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors through shared outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and shell-like tooling, so it may ingest external content; agent_b is non-egress and has no documented isolation or provenance controls. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, but agent_a’s MCP/stdio surface makes instruction smuggling plausible if B’s outputs are fed into it. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF agent_b outputs are copied into agent_a via MCP or stdin/stdout, then prompt injection is possible.
IF agent_a parses file or message content as instructions without provenance checks, then attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of B outputs into A.
Add provenance tags to all B-generated text.
Require a human review step before A executes instructions from B.
Restrict A’s MCP tools to read-only where possible.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and has allowlisted egress; agent_b has network_egress none and no data classes listed. There is no documented shared workspace or shared OAuth principal, so leakage is not evidenced as default. The main risk is limited to accidental transfer of A-held data into B-facing outputs.
conditions: IF agent_a is given sensitive repository content and its outputs are forwarded to B, then leakage can occur.
IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace, then A-held files may be exposed to B-side processing.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not forward raw A context to B.
Redact secrets before any handoff.
Audit egress allowlists for A.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, modify git state, install packages, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b has no write or network capabilities documented, so direct conflict is asymmetric. However, if both are orchestrated over the same repo or mutable workspace, A can race or overwrite shared state. The absence of locking evidence prevents a lower severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository checkout, then git and filesystem conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locks, then concurrent A instances can overwrite each other’s changes.
mitigations: Run A in a separate checkout.
Serialize write operations.
Disable git writes unless needed.
Use per-agent temp directories.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate outputs from prompts and repository data, while agent_b’s category and docs suggest it may consume or present AI-engineering content. There is no verification chain documented between them, so if B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream work products. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text without verification, then A’s mistakes can propagate.
IF A’s outputs are used as facts or citations by B, then downstream hallucinations can be rendered as authoritative.
mitigations: Require B to cite sources independently.
Add a verification checklist before B uses A output.
Mark A output as untrusted by default.
Limit A to draft-only roles.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware chaining.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. agent_a lists generic code and prompts; agent_b lists no data classes and no compliance surfaces. With no evidence of a mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF future documentation shows regulated data classes for either agent, reassess compliance risk.
IF a residency or retention policy is added later, compare it before deployment.
mitigations: Document data residency for both agents.
Record retention policies.
Classify any regulated inputs before use.
Avoid sending regulated data until reviewed.
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement.
